# Ready-to-paste statements for submission forms

## Declaration of competing interest
The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

## Funding
This research received no external funding.

## Ethics
This is a secondary analysis of publicly released, aggregated national statistics. No human participants were recruited and no personal data were collected; no ethics approval was required.

## Data availability (benchmark paper)
All inputs are public. The harmonised data (GovAlloc-COFOG v1.0) are archived on Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24248315 (v1.0: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24248316), with a mirror on Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/pranavchaudhari24/govalloc-cofog-government-spending-by-function). The original providers' terms apply to the underlying statistics.

## Code availability
Code, result files and LaTeX sources: https://github.com/Pranav-chaudhari-2006/GovAllocXAI, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24255442 (v1.0.0: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24255443), MIT licence.

## Declaration of generative AI use
During the preparation of this work the authors used Anthropic's Claude, an AI coding and writing assistant, for code scaffolding, data-collection scripts, drafting and editing of text, and for simulated critical review of the manuscript; the legacy dataset analysed in the audit section had itself been partly populated with the help of a large language model. References were checked with automated Crossref and arXiv lookups followed by manual correction. The authors reviewed and edited all content produced with these tools and take full responsibility for the content of the publication.

## Highlights (Elsevier: 3-5 bullets, max 85 characters each)
* Open official-data benchmark of government spending shares by function
* Last year's allocation is hard to beat; the learned gain is small and fragile
* Peers help without history on a wide panel, not robustly on a narrow one
* SHAP and LIME agree on direction more than on ranking
* Open data, code and a leakage audit of an earlier benchmark

## Keywords
government expenditure; COFOG; benchmark; explainable AI; SHAP; LIME; persistence baseline; data leakage
